headline: A strong Pacific storm brings widespread rain and gusty southeast winds tonight into Tuesday, with coastal flood warnings along the Strait of Juan de Fuca shore Tuesday, another round of rain and wind Wednesday night through Thursday, and a Flood Watch for the southern Olympics and southern Puget Sound from Wednesday through Sunday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: The main band of rain has been stalled over the coast and the nearby lowlands, including the north Olympic Peninsula, this evening and is creeping east only slowly, so it likely won't reach areas east of Puget Sound until overnight. Gusty southeast winds are increasing along with the rain, strongest in the San Juan Islands, Island County and along the coast, where there is better than an 80 percent chance of gusts over 40 mph; a Wind Advisory runs until 4 PM Tuesday for the coast and the western and southern Olympic foothills, with gusts near 35 mph at Hoquiam late tonight. Around Seattle, south-southeast winds of about 9–17 mph gust near 23 mph at times, and lows tonight range from the upper 30s to mid 40s. A Winter Weather Advisory continues for the Whatcom and Skagit County Cascades until 10 PM Tuesday.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Rain continues Tuesday, breaking into showers later in the day, before the storm's front moves out Tuesday evening, leaving lingering showers and breezy winds. Another system brings a fresh round of widespread rain and breezy winds Wednesday night into early Thursday, with snow levels rising well above the passes by Wednesday evening, so the mountains get rain rather than snow. A Flood Watch runs from Wednesday morning through Sunday afternoon for the Olympics and their western and southern foothills, southern Hood Canal, Olympia and the southern Puget Sound, the middle Chehalis River valley, and the Willapa and Black Hills; the Skokomish River will likely reach flood stage around midweek and could rise to moderate or even near major flooding, though no widespread river flooding is expected. Temperatures run above normal through Wednesday night, with highs in the low to mid 50s and lows well into the 40s.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Thursday's system moves out by evening but may first bring another round of gusty winds and widespread rain that could be moderate to heavy at times. Unsettled weather lingers into Friday, then high pressure may build over the weekend for a brief change to quieter weather, though forecasters are not yet sure how strong it will be or exactly where it sets up. Temperatures return closer to normal from Friday on.

coast: High surf combined with high tides brings hazardous coastal conditions this week, including major coastal flooding, peaking Tuesday, lasting into the second half of the week, and peaking again Thursday. On Tuesday, Coastal Flood Warnings run from 8 AM to 3 PM for the eastern and western Strait of Juan de Fuca (including the Sequim–Port Angeles shore), the north Washington coast and the Grays Harbor County coast, and from 2 AM to 4 PM for San Juan County; a Coastal Flood Advisory runs from 2 AM to 5 PM Tuesday for the Seattle, Shoreline–Lynnwood–Everett, Island County, Pierce and south King, Skagit–Snohomish and Whatcom shorelines. Tides become a concern for inland shorelines from Wednesday, with Coastal Flood Watches from late Tuesday night through Wednesday afternoon and again from late Wednesday night through Thursday afternoon covering the Strait, Port Townsend, Puget Sound from Seattle to Everett, eastern Kitsap County, northern Hood Canal, the San Juans, Island County and the coast. A High Surf Advisory covers the north Washington and Grays Harbor coasts from 10 AM Tuesday to 4 PM Wednesday. For boaters, until 11 PM Tuesday a Storm Warning covers the outer coastal waters (10–60 miles out), Gale Warnings cover the inner coastal waters and both the west and east entrances of the Strait, and Small Craft Advisories cover the central Strait (with a brief lull overnight before winds pick back up Tuesday), Admiralty Inlet, the northern inland waters and San Juan Islands, and the Grays Harbor bar. Another front Wednesday into Thursday could bring even stronger winds, likely more storm warnings on the outer waters and small craft to gale conditions elsewhere, with isolated afternoon thunderstorms possible over the coastal waters each day. Seas of 10–15 feet build to 18–25 feet by Tuesday afternoon, ease slightly but turn into longer-period swells Wednesday and Thursday, and drop below 10 feet Friday night into Saturday before building again to 8–12 feet by the end of the weekend; Friday brings a brief break from the wind before more windy systems next week.
watch_for: Coastal flooding at Tuesday's high tide along the Strait of Juan de Fuca (warning 8 AM–3 PM) and Puget Sound shorelines, with more coastal flood watches Wednesday and Thursday.
The Skokomish River, likely reaching flood stage midweek and possibly moderate to near-major flooding, under a Flood Watch from Wednesday morning through Sunday afternoon.
Whether high pressure really builds this weekend; its strength and placement are still uncertain.
confidence: Forecasters say tonight's forecast is on track and are confident in the wet, windy pattern with coastal flooding through Friday, but have low confidence in how strong and where the weekend high pressure sets up.
